correctness.rationale: For independent uniformly random k-subsets of n with k/n -> p in (0,1), two incidence columns collide per row with exact probability q_n. Factorial moment graph expansion: disjoint pairs contribute lambda^r, and nonmatching components s>=3 vanish since p^s+(1-p)^s < (p^2+(1-p)^2)^{s/2}. Thus Poisson X and lattice zero-collision CDF exp[-binom(n,2)q_n^t]. Expected unseen coupon n(1-k/n)^t -> 0 at the collision window, yielding Type II equality probability ->1 and expected delay o(1); collision second-moment lower tail plus first-moment upper tail establish E QI=b_n+O(1). Partition-lattice Mobius inversion proves exact finite formula. Independent enumeration of row sequences confirmed probabilities (n,k,t)=(3,1,2):2/3,(4,2,3):8/9,(5,2,3):12/25,(5,2,4):96/125. Boundary p->0 or1 intentionally excluded.

originality.rationale: Rényi 1961 Theorem 1 proves birthday-window and factor-two design overhead for independent fair coin-bit rows, i.e. random unrestricted-size subsets, and deserves priority for the phenomenon. A fixed row weight creates dependent incidence columns, so Rényi’s product identity does not imply the claimed factorial-moment Poisson limit. Tan et al 2025 define exactly this labeled coupon problem and stopping criteria, addressing deterministic designs and expected values (not dense-group Poisson window). No precise dependent-window prior located; qualified PASS restricted to fixed-size dense sampling theorem and Type II coupling.
residual_risks: Potential general Poisson approximation for dependent random separating codes implies fixed-cardinality special case.
Sampling fractions near endpoints are excluded, and integer-time lattice phases require exact handling.
